Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 28, verse 36–43:

﴿So when Musa came to them with Our signs, clear proofs, they said, "This is nothing but fabricated magic, and we never heard of this among our forefathers, the earliest ones."﴾ ﴿Musa said, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him, and who will have the good outcome of the abode. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾ ﴿Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than myself. So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look upon the god of Musa, though I think him to be among the liars."﴾ ﴿And he and his soldiers became arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.﴾ ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea. So see how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿And We made them leaders calling to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.﴾ ﴿And We followed them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.﴾ ﴿And We had certainly given Musa the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations as a source of insight for the people, and guidance and mercy, that they might remember.﴾

﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ (with Our signs) are the staff and the hand.

﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ means clear in indicating his truthfulness, and that it is an extraordinary, miraculous matter. They ceased resisting and opposing him, so they reverted to slander and lying, and attributed it to being magic, because they see a thing in one state, then see it in another state, then it returns to the first state. So they claimed that it was magic that Musa fabricates and attributes falsely to God, and therefore it is not a miracle. Then, together with their claim that it is fabricated magic, and their lie in that, they went further in lying, saying that they had never heard of this among their fathers, meaning in the time of their fathers and their days. And "among our fathers" is a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl), meaning "this," that is, something like this existing in the days of our fathers. When they denied hearing of the like of this in the earlier time, it became established that what Musa claimed is a novelty, to which nothing similar had preceded, and this indicates that it is fabricated against God. They were lying in that, and the means by which they heard reports of the earlier messengers, Musa being in their time. Do you not see the saying of a believer from the family of Pharaoh: ﴿And Joseph had certainly come to you before with clear proofs﴾ [Ghafir: 34]?

When Musa saw what they countered him with, namely that what he brought was magic, and the absence of hearing of the like in the earlier time, ﴿Musa said, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him"﴾, since He qualified him for prophethood, sent him with guidance, and promised him a good final outcome, and he means by this himself; and had he been as they claim, He would not have sent him. Then he drew attention to the cause that makes success impossible, which is wrongdoing (ẓulm), meaning placing a thing other than its place, since they were called to belief in God and brought miracles, yet they claimed divinity and attributed that miraculous matter to magic. The "outcome of the abode" (ʿāqibat al-dār), although it may apply to both the praiseworthy and the blameworthy, has been used most often for the praiseworthy, so if it is not restricted, it is understood in that sense. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Those will have the good outcome of the abode﴾ [al-Ra'd: 22], ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23]? And He said: ﴿And the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the good outcome of the abode﴾ [al-Ra'd: 42]. Ibn Kathir recited "Qāla Mūsā" without a waw; the rest of the seven read it with the waw. The rationale for the majority reading is that when he brought them the clear proofs, they said "such and such," and Musa said "such and such," so the observer distinguishes the difference between the two statements and the corruption of one of them, since they stand opposed, and thus he knows with certainty that the statement of Musa is the truth and guidance. The rationale for Ibn Kathir's reading is that it is a place of recitation: when they said "such and such," Musa said "such and such."

Pharaoh denied to his chiefs that he knew of a god other than himself, intending by this the negation of its existence, meaning: you have no god other than me. It is also possible that a god for them was not known to him, but was only supposed, so the negation is on its apparent meaning. This is indicated by his saying: ﴿And I think him to be among the liars﴾, and he was lying in the negation of his knowledge of a god other than himself. Do you not see his saying at the time of his drowning: ﴿I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾ [Yunus: 90]? Pharaoh continued in his deception, called his minister Haman, and ordered him to kindle fire upon the clay. It was said: he was the first to make baked brick, and he did not say "bake the brick," because Haman had no prior knowledge of that, so Pharaoh is the one who teaches him what to do.

﴿فاجْعَلْ لِي صَرْحًا﴾ means build for me, ﴿that I may look upon the god of Musa﴾. He gave his people the impression that the god of Musa can be reached and overcome, while he, knowing with certainty that this is impossible for him, yet because of his people's foolishness, ignorance, and extreme blindness, it was possible in their eyes; and the very region of Egypt requires of its people belief in impossibilities and susceptibility to illusions and imaginings. There is no doubt that among Pharaoh's people there were those who believed his claim to be false, but agreed with him out of fear of his power and aggression, just as we have seen it happen to many intelligent people when a chief in their presence narrates an impossible story, they agree with him about that story. The command to build the tower does not indicate that it was built, and this has been disputed: it was said, he built it, and one who described it mentioned things that God alone knows; and it was said, it was not built. Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 28, verses 44–50 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses.﴾ ﴿But We produced generations, and the lifetime grew long for them. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting Our verses to them, but We were ever sending messengers.﴾ ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called out, but it was a mercy from your Lord, that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that perhaps they might be mindful.﴾ ﴿And had it not been that a misfortune might befall them because of what their hands had sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs and be among the believers?"﴾ ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, "Two sorceries backing each other," and they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in both."﴾ ﴿Say, "Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guided than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

When Allah (Exalted) had related the accounts of Moses and the remarkable events that befell him, namely his being conceived at the time when the sons were being slaughtered, his being cast into the sea in a chest, his being returned to his mother, Pharaoh's adoption of him, his being granted judgment and knowledge, his killing of the Copt, his leaving his homeland in flight, his marriage connection with Shu'ayb, his tending of Shu'ayb's sheep for many long years, his return to Egypt, his losing the way, Allah's conversing with him, the manifesting through his hands of those two great miracles, namely the staff and the hand, his being commanded to go to Pharaoh, his dialogue with him, Pharaoh's denial and his destruction along with his people, and the favour bestowed upon Moses in giving him the Torah, Allah (Exalted) revealed all of that to Muhammad, His Messenger (ﷺ). He reminded him of His bounty upon him in this regard, and of the unseen matters that He had specially granted him, which neither he nor his people had known. So He said: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command.﴾

As for "al-amr" (the command), it has been said: it is prophethood and the judgment that Allah gave Moses. It has also been said: the command is the command to Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he should be among his community, and this interpretation harmonises with what follows it, His saying: ﴿But We produced generations.﴾ It has also been said: the command is the destruction of Pharaoh by water, and "bi-janib al-gharbi" (on the western side) is to be understood as the sea (al-yamm).

He began first by negating a specific matter, which is that he was not present (p-122) at the time when Allah decreed the command to Moses. Then he repeated it by saying that he was not among the witnesses. The meaning, and Allah knows best, is: not among the witnesses to all that We informed you of. Thus it is a negation of his witnessing all that happened to Moses, so it was a generality after a specification.

As for "bi-janib al-gharbi": according to some, it is an idafa (construct) of the qualified noun to its qualifier; according to others, the noun has been omitted and the qualifier put in its place. On the first view the original is "bi-l-janib al-gharbi," and on the second the original is "bi-janib al-makan al-gharbi." The preference between the two views is mentioned in grammar (nahw).

As for "al-gharbi": Qatadah said it is the western side of the mountain. Al-Hasan said: Allah sent Moses to the west. Abu 'Ubaydah said: the place where the sun, the moon and the stars set. It has been said: here there is a western mountain. It has been said: al-gharbi is of the valley, and it has been said: of the sea.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: the meaning is: you, O Muhammad, were not present at these unseen matters about which you are informed, but they came to you by Our revelation. That is to say, it was incumbent that one should hasten to believe in you, but the matter stretched over the generations which We produced age after age, so their wisdom faded and their ignorance and error became firmly established.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-gharb is the place lying on the western side, which is the place where Moses' appointed time on the Mount occurred, and where Allah wrote for him on the tablets. The command decreed to Moses is the revelation that was revealed to him. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: you were not present at the place where We revealed to Moses, nor were you among the company of those who witnessed the revelation to him, or [witnessing] upon the revelation to him, namely his deputies whom he chose for the appointed time, so that you might learn from the body of the witnesses what happened to Moses at his appointed time, the writing of the Torah for him on the tablets, and other things.

(If you ask): how does His saying ﴿But We produced generations﴾ connect with this statement, and in what respect is it a corrective (istidrak) to it? (I answer): its connection to it and its being a corrective lies in the fact that its meaning is: But We produced, after the era of the revelation until your era, many generations, so the lifetime stretched over the last of them, and that is the generation in which you exist.

﴿The lifetime grew long﴾: that is, the period of the cessation of revelation, and the sciences were effaced, so it became necessary to send you to them. So We sent you and taught you knowledge of the stories of the prophets and the story of Moses. It is as if He said: you were not a witness to Moses and what happened to him, but We revealed it to you. Thus He mentioned the cause of the revelation, which is the lengthening of the interval, and indicated the effect through it, in accordance with Allah's custom of brevity. Therefore this istidrak (corrective statement) resembles the two istidraks after it.

﴿And you were not dwelling﴾: that is, residing among the people of Madyan, who were Shu'ayb and the believers.

﴿Reciting to them Our verses﴾: reading to them, learning from them, meaning the verses in which is the story of Shu'ayb and his people. But We sent you and informed you of them and taught them to you.

﴿When We called out﴾: he means the calling out to Moses on the night of the secret conversation and speaking with him. But We taught you. It has been said: ﴿So the lifetime grew long for them﴾ and prophethood became dormant, the laws were effaced, and much of them was distorted. The completion of the statement is implied, and its estimate is: We sent you renewing those reports, distinguishing the truth from what had been disputed among them, as a mercy from Us. It has been said: it is possible that the meaning is: you were not among the witnesses at that time, and between you and Moses there were generations whose lifetimes stretched long, and you now relate those circumstances by way of direct witnessing and vision, through Our inspiration to you as a miracle for you. It has been said: "tatlu" (reciting) is a circumstantial clause (hal), and it has been said: it is a new independent statement, meaning: you now recite the story of Shu'ayb, but We sent you as a messenger, and We sent down to you a Book in which these forgotten reports are contained, which you recite to them, and had it not been for you, I would not have informed them of what they did not witness.

Al-Farra' said: ﴿And you were not dwelling﴾ among the people of Madyan with Moses, so that you would see him and hear his speech, and now you are ﴿reciting to them Our verses﴾, that is, to your community, so it is disconnected [from what precedes]. End of quotation. It has been said: if he was not present at that place, then what is the meaning of ﴿nor were you among the witnesses﴾? Ibn 'Abbas said: the estimate is: you did not attend that place, and even had you attended, you would not have witnessed those events, for it is possible that there was [someone] there who would neither witness nor see. Muqatil said: he did not witness the people of Madyan so as to read their report to the people of Makkah, but We sent you to the people of Makkah, and sent down to you these reports, and had it not been for that, you would not have known. Al-Dahhak said: he says: you, O Muhammad, were not the messenger to the people of Madyan, reciting to them the verses of the Book, but rather it was another, (p-123) but We were ever sending a messenger in every age: We sent Shu'ayb to Madyan, and We sent you to the Arabs so that you would be the seal of the prophets. End of quotation.

Al-Tabari said: ﴿When We called out﴾ with [the words]: "I will write it for those who fear [Me]." And from Abu Hurayrah: that at that time a voice was called out from heaven: "O community of Muhammad, I have answered you before you called upon Me, and I have forgiven you before you asked Me." Then Moses (peace be upon him) said: "O Allah, make me of the community of Muhammad." So the meaning is: when We called out by Your command, and We informed you of your prophethood.

The majority read ﴿mercy﴾ in the accusative (raḥmatan), so it is estimated: "but We made you a mercy," and it is estimated: We informed you and made you aware as a mercy. 'Isa and Abu Haywah read it in the nominative (raḥmatun), and they estimated: "but he is a mercy," or "he is a mercy," or "you are a mercy."

﴿That you might warn a people to whom no warner had come﴾: that is, in the period of the interval between you and 'Isa, which is about five hundred and fifty years or so. The answer to (lawla) is omitted. The meaning is: had it not been that they would say, when they are punished for what they had sent forth of polytheism and sins, "Why did You not send to us a messenger?", arguing with that against us, [We sent messengers]. That is: We only sent the messengers to remove this excuse, as He said: ﴿So that there would not be for people any argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165], and [so that] you would not say: ﴿There came to us no bringer of good tidings nor warner﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 19]. The estimate of the answer is: We did not send messengers to them, this is the statement of al-Zajjaj. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: its estimate is: We would have hastened to punish them with what they deserve.

The misfortune (muṣība) is the punishment. Since most actions are performed by the hands, every deed was expressed by the earning of the hands, even deeds of the hearts, as an extension of speech, and making the minority follow the majority, and giving the majority precedence over the minority.

The fa' in ﴿fa-yaqulu﴾ is for conjunction with "tuṣība" [it might befall them]; the second lawla is for urging (taḥḍīḍ). And in "fa-nattabi'a" the fa' is the answer to the urging.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you ask): how is this meaning valid, when the punishment has been made the cause of the sending, not the saying, since the particle of prevention (ḥarf al-imtina') enters upon it and not upon the saying? (I answer): the saying is what is intended, so that it would be the cause of the sending of the messengers, but since the punishment was the cause of the saying, its existence was dependent upon its existence. The punishment was made as if it were the cause of the sending through the medium of the saying. Thus lawla was placed before it, and the saying was brought joined to it by the fa' which gives the meaning of causation. Its meaning reduces to your saying: "And had it not been for their saying this, ﴿when a misfortune befalls them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 156], We would not have sent [messengers]." But this method was chosen for a subtle reason, which is that they were not punished, for example, for their disbelief, while they had seen what they were compelled by to the certain knowledge. They did not say: "Why did You not send to us a messenger?", and the cause of this saying of theirs is only the punishment and nothing else, not regret over what they missed of faith in their Creator. In this there is, of the strong testimony to the firmness and deep-rootedness of their disbelief, what is not hidden, like their saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would go back to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. End of quotation.

As for "al-Haqq" (the Truth): it is the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who came with the inimitable Book which cut off their excuses. It has been said: it is the Qur'an.

﴿Like what was given to Moses﴾. ﴿Before﴾: that is, before the Book that was sent down all at once, and the turning of the staff into a serpent, the splitting of the sea, and other signs. They proposed that out of obstinacy and stubbornness, just as they said: "Why was not a treasure sent down upon him?" and other such proposals they made. This statement that they uttered is from the teaching of the Jews to the Quraysh; they said to them: "Will he not bring a manifest sign like the signs of Moses?" So Allah answered them that they disbelieved in the signs of Moses, and what occurred from them concerning the signs of Moses is what occurred from these [people] concerning the signs of the Messenger.

The pronoun in ﴿Did they not disbelieve﴾ refers to the Jews, as Ibn 'Atiyyah said. It has been said: the speaker of that is the Arabs, by instruction, as we have said. It has been said: the speaker of that is the Jews. It appears to me that it refers to the Quraysh, who said: "Why was he not given (*lawla ūtiya*)," meaning Muhammad, "the like of what was given to Moses?" That is because their denial of Muhammad (ﷺ) is a denial of Moses (peace be upon him), and their attribution of sorcery to the Messenger is like their attribution of sorcery to Moses, since the prophets are of one valley. Whoever attributes to one of the prophets what is not fitting has attributed it to all the prophets. All the pronouns harmonise in this, in His saying: ﴿Say, "Then bring a Book from Allah"﴾. Although the apparent meaning of "qala" (saying) is verbal utterance, it may also apply to belief, and they, in terms of denying prophethoods, believed that what appeared at the hands of the prophets of signs was only a kind of sorcery.

(p-124) Al-Zamakhshari said: "Awa lam yakfuru" (Did they not disbelieve) means the fathers of their kind, and whoever holds their creed shares their creed, and their obstinacy is their obstinacy; they are the disbelievers of the time of Musa, "bima utiya Musa" (in what was given to Musa). And from al-Hasan: there was already a basis among the Arabs in the days of Musa, so its meaning according to this is: Did not their fathers disbelieve? They said of Musa and Harun: "Two sorceries that back each other up" (saahiran tazaharaa), that is, they cooperated. End of quotation. "Min qablu" (before): it may be connected to "yakfuru" and to "utiya."

The majority read: "saahiran" (two sorcerers). Mujahid said: Musa and Harun. Al-Hasan said: Musa and Isa. Ibn Abbas said: Musa and Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-Hasan also said: Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud], Zayd ibn Ali, and the Kufans read: "sihraan" (two magics). Ibn Abbas said: the Torah and the Qur'an. It was also said: the Torah and the Injil, or Musa and Harun were called two magics as a form of emphasis.

"Tazaharaa" means they cooperated. The majority read "tazaharaa" as a past verb on the pattern of tafaa'ala. Talhah and al-A'mash read "izzaharaa" with a hamzat al-wasl and a shaddah on the zay, and likewise it is in the reading of Abdullah; its original form is "tazaharaa," and the ta' was assimilated into the za', so a hamzat al-wasl was brought in because of the sukun of the assimilated ta'. Mahbub from al-Hasan, Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Dhimari, Abu Haywa, and Abu Khallad from al-Yazidi read "tazzaharaa" with a ta' and a shaddah on the za'. Ibn Khalawayh said: its shaddah is a grammatical error, because it is a past verb, and the shaddah is only used in the present tense. Sahib al-Lawami said: I do not know its basis. Sahib al-Kamil fi al-Qira'at said: it has no meaning. End of quotation. However, it has an explanation in the language: it is a present tense verb from which the nun has been dropped, and the dropping of it has occurred in a few instances in speech and in poetry. "Saahiran" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "antuma saahiraani tatazaharaani" (you two are two sorcerers who back each other up); then the ta' was assimilated into the za' and the nun was dropped, and the pronoun of address was observed. If it were read "yazzaharaa" with a ya', taking into account "saahiraan," it would have a basis, or by estimating "they two are sorcerers that back each other up."

"Wa qaluu inna bikullin kaafiruun" (And they said: Indeed we disbelieve in each of them), that is, in each of the two sorcerers or the two sorceries. Then Allah commanded him to proclaim this verse, which is His saying: "Qul fa'tuu" (Say: Then bring), that is, you, O deniers of these books, which contain the command to acts of worship and noble character, forbid disbelief and blameworthy traits, and for which Allah promised great reward. "If your denial is for some reason, then bring a Book from Allah which gives better guidance than these two, I will follow it with you." The pronoun in "minhaa" refers to what was revealed to Musa and to Muhammad (ﷺ) (may Allah bless them both and grant them peace). Making their bringing of such a book conditional on truthfulness is a matter that is certain and established: it will not happen, and their truthfulness is impossible, just as it is impossible that they bring a Book from Allah that is more guided than the two Books. It is also permissible that the condition is intended as mockery of them. Zayd ibn Ali read "atta'bi'uhu" with a raf' on the 'ayn as a new sentence, meaning: I follow it.

"Fa-in lam yastajiibuu laka" (And if they do not respond to you). Ibn Abbas said: it means if they do not believe in what you have brought of proofs, and they are not able to bring a Book that is better. Istijabah (responding) implies a call, and he (ﷺ) always calls to faith; that is, if they do not respond to you after the miracles contained in your Book that was revealed have become clear to them. Or the saying "fa'tuu bikitab" may itself be the call, since it is a request from them and a call upon them to bring it. It is known that they will not respond by bringing a Book from Allah. So know that they have nothing but the following of mere desire, not the following of evidence. "Istajaba" means "ajaba," and it is transitive to the one called with "li" and without it, as He said: "Fastajaba lahu rabbuhu" (Yusuf 34), "Fastajabnaa lahu wa wahabnaa lahu Yahyaa" (al-Anbiya 90), "Fa-in lam yastajiibuu lakum" (Hud 14). The poet said:

"Fa lam yastajibhu 'inda dhaalika mujiibu"
So he transitively used it without "li." Al-Zamakhshari said: this verb is transitive to the call and to the one called with "li," and the call is usually omitted when it is transitive to the one called, so one says: "Istajaba Allahu du'aahu" and "istajaba lahu," but one hardly says "istajaba lahu du'aahu." As for the verse, its meaning is: "lam yastajib du'aa'," with the omission of the modifier. End of quotation.

"Wa man adallu" (And who is more astray), that is, no one is more astray. "Bi-ghayri hudan" (without guidance) is in the position of a circumstantial clause, and this circumstance is a restriction on following desire, because a person may follow what he desires, and that which he desires may contain guidance from Allah, since all desires are divided into those that contain guidance (p-125) and those that do not contain guidance; therefore it is restricted by this circumstance. Al-Zamakhshari said: meaning forsaken, left to his own desire. End of quotation, and this is according to the path of the Mu'tazila.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 28, verses 44–50 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses.﴾ ﴿But We produced generations, and the lifetime grew long for them. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting Our verses to them, but We were ever sending messengers.﴾ ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called out, but it was a mercy from your Lord, that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that perhaps they might be mindful.﴾ ﴿And had it not been that a misfortune might befall them because of what their hands had sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs and be among the believers?"﴾ ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, "Two sorceries backing each other," and they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in both."﴾ ﴿Say, "Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guided than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

When Allah (Exalted) had related the accounts of Moses and the remarkable events that befell him, namely his being conceived at the time when the sons were being slaughtered, his being cast into the sea in a chest, his being returned to his mother, Pharaoh's adoption of him, his being granted judgment and knowledge, his killing of the Copt, his leaving his homeland in flight, his marriage connection with Shu'ayb, his tending of Shu'ayb's sheep for many long years, his return to Egypt, his losing the way, Allah's conversing with him, the manifesting through his hands of those two great miracles, namely the staff and the hand, his being commanded to go to Pharaoh, his dialogue with him, Pharaoh's denial and his destruction along with his people, and the favour bestowed upon Moses in giving him the Torah, Allah (Exalted) revealed all of that to Muhammad, His Messenger (ﷺ). He reminded him of His bounty upon him in this regard, and of the unseen matters that He had specially granted him, which neither he nor his people had known. So He said: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command.﴾

As for "al-amr" (the command), it has been said: it is prophethood and the judgment that Allah gave Moses. It has also been said: the command is the command to Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he should be among his community, and this interpretation harmonises with what follows it, His saying: ﴿But We produced generations.﴾ It has also been said: the command is the destruction of Pharaoh by water, and "bi-janib al-gharbi" (on the western side) is to be understood as the sea (al-yamm).

He began first by negating a specific matter, which is that he was not present (p-122) at the time when Allah decreed the command to Moses. Then he repeated it by saying that he was not among the witnesses. The meaning, and Allah knows best, is: not among the witnesses to all that We informed you of. Thus it is a negation of his witnessing all that happened to Moses, so it was a generality after a specification.

As for "bi-janib al-gharbi": according to some, it is an idafa (construct) of the qualified noun to its qualifier; according to others, the noun has been omitted and the qualifier put in its place. On the first view the original is "bi-l-janib al-gharbi," and on the second the original is "bi-janib al-makan al-gharbi." The preference between the two views is mentioned in grammar (nahw).

As for "al-gharbi": Qatadah said it is the western side of the mountain. Al-Hasan said: Allah sent Moses to the west. Abu 'Ubaydah said: the place where the sun, the moon and the stars set. It has been said: here there is a western mountain. It has been said: al-gharbi is of the valley, and it has been said: of the sea.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: the meaning is: you, O Muhammad, were not present at these unseen matters about which you are informed, but they came to you by Our revelation. That is to say, it was incumbent that one should hasten to believe in you, but the matter stretched over the generations which We produced age after age, so their wisdom faded and their ignorance and error became firmly established.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-gharb is the place lying on the western side, which is the place where Moses' appointed time on the Mount occurred, and where Allah wrote for him on the tablets. The command decreed to Moses is the revelation that was revealed to him. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: you were not present at the place where We revealed to Moses, nor were you among the company of those who witnessed the revelation to him, or [witnessing] upon the revelation to him, namely his deputies whom he chose for the appointed time, so that you might learn from the body of the witnesses what happened to Moses at his appointed time, the writing of the Torah for him on the tablets, and other things.

(If you ask): how does His saying ﴿But We produced generations﴾ connect with this statement, and in what respect is it a corrective (istidrak) to it? (I answer): its connection to it and its being a corrective lies in the fact that its meaning is: But We produced, after the era of the revelation until your era, many generations, so the lifetime stretched over the last of them, and that is the generation in which you exist.

﴿The lifetime grew long﴾: that is, the period of the cessation of revelation, and the sciences were effaced, so it became necessary to send you to them. It is as if He said: you were not a witness to Moses and what happened to him, but We revealed it to you. Talhah and al-A'mash read "izzaharaa" with a hamzat al-wasl and a shaddah on the zay, and likewise it is in the reading of Abdullah; its original form is "tazaharaa," and the ta' was assimilated into the za', so a hamzat al-wasl was brought in because of the sukun of the assimilated ta'. Mahbub from al-Hasan, Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Dhimari, Abu Haywa, and Abu Khallad from al-Yazidi read "tazzaharaa" with a ta' and a shaddah on the za'. Ibn Khalawayh said: its shaddah is a grammatical error, because it is a past verb, and the shaddah is only used in the present tense. Sahib al-Lawami said: I do not know its basis. Sahib al-Kamil fi al-Qira'at said: it has no meaning. End of quotation. However, it has an explanation in the language: it is a present tense verb from which the nun has been dropped, and the dropping of it has occurred in a few instances in speech and in poetry. "Saahiran" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "antuma saahiraani tatazaharaani" (you two are two sorcerers who back each other up); then the ta' was assimilated into the za' and the nun was dropped, and the pronoun of address was observed. If it were read "yazzaharaa" with a ya', taking into account "saahiraan," it would have a basis, or by estimating "they two are sorcerers that back each other up."

"Wa qaluu inna bikullin kaafiruun" (And they said: Indeed we disbelieve in each of them), that is, in each of the two sorcerers or the two sorceries. Then Allah commanded him to proclaim this verse, which is His saying: "Qul fa'tuu" (Say: Then bring), that is, you, O deniers of these books, which contain the command to acts of worship and noble character, forbid disbelief and blameworthy traits, and for which Allah promised great reward. "If your denial is for some reason, then bring a Book from Allah which gives better guidance than these two, I will follow it with you." The pronoun in "minhaa" refers to what was revealed to Musa and to Muhammad (ﷺ) (may Allah bless them both and grant them peace). Making their bringing of such a book conditional on truthfulness is a matter that is certain and established: it will not happen, and their truthfulness is impossible, just as it is impossible that they bring a Book from Allah that is more guided than the two Books. It is also permissible that the condition is intended as mockery of them. Zayd ibn Ali read "atta'bi'uhu" with a raf' on the 'ayn as a new sentence, meaning: I follow it.

"Fa-in lam yastajiibuu laka" (And if they do not respond to you). Ibn Abbas said: it means if they do not believe in what you have brought of proofs, and they are not able to bring a Book that is better. Istijabah (responding) implies a call, and he (ﷺ) always calls to faith; that is, if they do not respond to you after the miracles contained in your Book that was revealed have become clear to them. Or the saying "fa'tuu bikitab" may itself be the call, since it is a request from them and a call upon them to bring it. It is known that they will not respond by bringing a Book from Allah. So know that they have nothing but the following of mere desire, not the following of evidence. "Istajaba" means "ajaba," and it is transitive to the one called with "li" and without it, as He said: "Fastajaba lahu rabbuhu" (Yusuf 34), "Fastajabnaa lahu wa wahabnaa lahu Yahyaa" (al-Anbiya 90), "Fa-in lam yastajiibuu lakum" (Hud 14). The poet said:

"Fa lam yastajibhu 'inda dhaalika mujiibu"
So he transitively used it without "li." Al-Zamakhshari said: this verb is transitive to the call and to the one called with "li," and the call is usually omitted when it is transitive to the one called, so one says: "Istajaba Allahu du'aahu" and "istajaba lahu," but one hardly says "istajaba lahu du'aahu." As for the verse, its meaning is: "lam yastajib du'aa'," with the omission of the modifier. End of quotation.

"Wa man adallu" (And who is more astray), that is, no one is more astray. "Bi-ghayri hudan" (without guidance) is in the position of a circumstantial clause, and this circumstance is a restriction on following desire, because a person may follow what he desires, and that which he desires may contain guidance from Allah, since all desires are divided into those that contain guidance (p-125) and those that do not contain guidance; therefore it is restricted by this circumstance. Al-Zamakhshari said: meaning forsaken, left to his own desire. End of quotation, and this is according to the path of the Mu'tazila.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 28, verses 44–50 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses.﴾ ﴿But We produced generations, and the lifetime grew long for them. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting Our verses to them, but We were ever sending messengers.﴾ ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called out, but it was a mercy from your Lord, that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that perhaps they might be mindful.﴾ ﴿And had it not been that a misfortune might befall them because of what their hands had sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs and be among the believers?"﴾ ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, "Two sorceries backing each other," and they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in both."﴾ ﴿Say, "Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guided than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

When Allah (Exalted) had related the accounts of Moses and the remarkable events that befell him, namely his being conceived at the time when the sons were being slaughtered, his being cast into the sea in a chest, his being returned to his mother, Pharaoh's adoption of him, his being granted judgment and knowledge, his killing of the Copt, his leaving his homeland in flight, his marriage connection with Shu'ayb, his tending of Shu'ayb's sheep for many long years, his return to Egypt, his losing the way, Allah's conversing with him, the manifesting through his hands of those two great miracles, namely the staff and the hand, his being commanded to go to Pharaoh, his dialogue with him, Pharaoh's denial and his destruction along with his people, and the favour bestowed upon Moses in giving him the Torah, Allah (Exalted) revealed all of that to Muhammad, His Messenger (ﷺ). He reminded him of His bounty upon him in this regard, and of the unseen matters that He had specially granted him, which neither he nor his people had known. So He said: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command.﴾

As for "al-amr" (the command), it has been said: it is prophethood and the judgment that Allah gave Moses. It has also been said: the command is the command to Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he should be among his community, and this interpretation harmonises with what follows it, His saying: ﴿But We produced generations.﴾ It has also been said: the command is the destruction of Pharaoh by water, and "bi-janib al-gharbi" (on the western side) is to be understood as the sea (al-yamm).

He began first by negating a specific matter, which is that he was not present (p-122) at the time when Allah decreed the command to Moses. Then he repeated it by saying that he was not among the witnesses. The meaning, and Allah knows best, is: not among the witnesses to all that We informed you of. Thus it is a negation of his witnessing all that happened to Moses, so it was a generality after a specification.

As for "bi-janib al-gharbi": according to some, it is an idafa (construct) of the qualified noun to its qualifier; according to others, the noun has been omitted and the qualifier put in its place. On the first view the original is "bi-l-janib al-gharbi," and on the second the original is "bi-janib al-makan al-gharbi." The preference between the two views is mentioned in grammar (nahw).

As for "al-gharbi": Qatadah said it is the western side of the mountain. Al-Hasan said: Allah sent Moses to the west. Abu 'Ubaydah said: the place where the sun, the moon and the stars set. It has been said: here there is a western mountain. It has been said: al-gharbi is of the valley, and it has been said: of the sea.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: the meaning is: you, O Muhammad, were not present at these unseen matters about which you are informed, but they came to you by Our revelation. That is to say, it was incumbent that one should hasten to believe in you, but the matter stretched over the generations which We produced age after age, so their wisdom faded and their ignorance and error became firmly established.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-gharb is the place lying on the western side, which is the place where Moses' appointed time on the Mount occurred, and where Allah wrote for him on the tablets. The command decreed to Moses is the revelation that was revealed to him. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: you were not present at the place where We revealed to Moses, nor were you among the company of those who witnessed the revelation to him, or [witnessing] upon the revelation to him, namely his deputies whom he chose for the appointed time, so that you might learn from the body of the witnesses what happened to Moses at his appointed time, the writing of the Torah for him on the tablets, and other things.

(If you ask): how does His saying ﴿But We produced generations﴾ connect with this statement, and in what respect is it a corrective (istidrak) to it? (I answer): its connection to it and its being a corrective lies in the fact that its meaning is: But We produced, after the era of the revelation until your era, many generations, so the lifetime stretched over the last of them, and that is the generation in which you exist.

﴿The lifetime grew long﴾: that is, the period of the cessation of revelation, and the sciences were effaced, so it became necessary to send you to them. So We sent you and taught you knowledge of the stories of the prophets and the story of Moses. It is as if He said: you were not a witness to Moses and what happened to him, but We revealed it to you. Thus He mentioned the cause of the revelation, which is the lengthening of the interval, and indicated the effect through it, in accordance with Allah's custom of brevity. Therefore this istidrak (corrective statement) resembles the two istidraks after it.

﴿And you were not dwelling﴾: that is, residing among the people of Madyan, who were Shu'ayb and the believers.

﴿Reciting to them Our verses﴾: reading to them, learning from them, meaning the verses in which is the story of Shu'ayb and his people. But We sent you and informed you of them and taught them to you.

﴿When We called out﴾: he means the calling out to Moses on the night of the secret conversation and speaking with him. But We taught you. It has been said: ﴿So the lifetime grew long for them﴾ and prophethood became dormant, the laws were effaced, and much of them was distorted. The completion of the statement is implied, and its estimate is: We sent you renewing those reports, distinguishing the truth from what had been disputed among them, as a mercy from Us. It has been said: it is possible that the meaning is: you were not among the witnesses at that time, and between you and Moses there were generations whose lifetimes stretched long, and you now relate those circumstances by way of direct witnessing and vision, through Our inspiration to you as a miracle for you. It has been said: "tatlu" (reciting) is a circumstantial clause (hal), and it has been said: it is a new independent statement, meaning: you now recite the story of Shu'ayb, but We sent you as a messenger, and We sent down to you a Book in which these forgotten reports are contained, which you recite to them, and had it not been for you, I would not have informed them of what they did not witness.

Al-Farra' said: ﴿And you were not dwelling﴾ among the people of Madyan with Moses, so that you would see him and hear his speech, and now you are ﴿reciting to them Our verses﴾, that is, to your community, so it is disconnected [from what precedes]. End of quotation. It has been said: if he was not present at that place, then what is the meaning of ﴿nor were you among the witnesses﴾? Ibn 'Abbas said: the estimate is: you did not attend that place, and even had you attended, you would not have witnessed those events, for it is possible that there was [someone] there who would neither witness nor see. Muqatil said: he did not witness the people of Madyan so as to read their report to the people of Makkah, but We sent you to the people of Makkah, and sent down to you these reports, and had it not been for that, you would not have known. Al-Dahhak said: he says: you, O Muhammad, were not the messenger to the people of Madyan, reciting to them the verses of the Book, but rather it was another, (p-123) but We were ever sending a messenger in every age: We sent Shu'ayb to Madyan, and We sent you to the Arabs so that you would be the seal of the prophets. End of quotation.

Al-Tabari said: ﴿When We called out﴾ with [the words]: "I will write it for those who fear [Me]." And from Abu Hurayrah: that at that time a voice was called out from heaven: "O community of Muhammad, I have answered you before you called upon Me, and I have forgiven you before you asked Me." Then Moses (peace be upon him) said: "O Allah, make me of the community of Muhammad." So the meaning is: when We called out by Your command, and We informed you of your prophethood.

The majority read ﴿mercy﴾ in the accusative (raḥmatan), so it is estimated: "but We made you a mercy," and it is estimated: We informed you and made you aware as a mercy. 'Isa and Abu Haywah read it in the nominative (raḥmatun), and they estimated: "but he is a mercy," or "he is a mercy," or "you are a mercy."

﴿That you might warn a people to whom no warner had come﴾: that is, in the period of the interval between you and 'Isa, which is about five hundred and fifty years or so. The answer to (lawla) is omitted. The meaning is: had it not been that they would say, when they are punished for what they had sent forth of polytheism and sins, "Why did You not send to us a messenger?", arguing with that against us, [We sent messengers]. That is: We only sent the messengers to remove this excuse, as He said: ﴿So that there would not be for people any argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165], and [so that] you would not say: ﴿There came to us no bringer of good tidings nor warner﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 19]. The estimate of the answer is: We did not send messengers to them, this is the statement of al-Zajjaj. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: its estimate is: We would have hastened to punish them with what they deserve.

The misfortune (muṣība) is the punishment. Since most actions are performed by the hands, every deed was expressed by the earning of the hands, even deeds of the hearts, as an extension of speech, and making the minority follow the majority, and giving the majority precedence over the minority.

The fa' in ﴿fa-yaqulu﴾ is for conjunction with "tuṣība" [it might befall them]; the second lawla is for urging (taḥḍīḍ). And in "fa-nattabi'a" the fa' is the answer to the urging.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you ask): how is this meaning valid, when the punishment has been made the cause of the sending, not the saying, since the particle of prevention (ḥarf al-imtina') enters upon it and not upon the saying? (I answer): the saying is what is intended, so that it would be the cause of the sending of the messengers, but since the punishment was the cause of the saying, its existence was dependent upon its existence. The punishment was made as if it were the cause of the sending through the medium of the saying. Thus lawla was placed before it, and the saying was brought joined to it by the fa' which gives the meaning of causation. Its meaning reduces to your saying: "And had it not been for their saying this, ﴿when a misfortune befalls them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 156], We would not have sent [messengers]." But this method was chosen for a subtle reason, which is that they were not punished, for example, for their disbelief, while they had seen what they were compelled by to the certain knowledge. They did not say: "Why did You not send to us a messenger?", and the cause of this saying of theirs is only the punishment and nothing else, not regret over what they missed of faith in their Creator. In this there is, of the strong testimony to the firmness and deep-rootedness of their disbelief, what is not hidden, like their saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would go back to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. End of quotation.

As for "al-Haqq" (the Truth): it is the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who came with the inimitable Book which cut off their excuses. It has been said: it is the Qur'an.

﴿Like what was given to Moses﴾. ﴿Before﴾: that is, before the Book that was sent down all at once, and the turning of the staff into a serpent, the splitting of the sea, and other signs. They proposed that out of obstinacy and stubbornness, just as they said: "Why was not a treasure sent down upon him?" and other such proposals they made. This statement that they uttered is from the teaching of the Jews to the Quraysh; they said to them: "Will he not bring a manifest sign like the signs of Moses?" So Allah answered them that they disbelieved in the signs of Moses, and what occurred from them concerning the signs of Moses is what occurred from these [people] concerning the signs of the Messenger.

The pronoun in ﴿Did they not disbelieve﴾ refers to the Jews, as Ibn 'Atiyyah said. It has been said: the speaker of that is the Arabs, by instruction, as we have said. It has been said: the speaker of that is the Jews. It appears to me that it refers to the Quraysh, who said: "Why was he not given (*lawla ūtiya*)," meaning Muhammad, "the like of what was given to Moses?" That is because their denial of Muhammad (ﷺ) is a denial of Moses (peace be upon him), and their attribution of sorcery to the Messenger is like their attribution of sorcery to Moses, since the prophets are of one valley. Whoever attributes to one of the prophets what is not fitting has attributed it to all the prophets. All the pronouns harmonise in this, in His saying: ﴿Say, "Then bring a Book from Allah"﴾. Although the apparent meaning of "qala" (saying) is verbal utterance, it may also apply to belief, and they, in terms of denying prophethoods, believed that what appeared at the hands of the prophets of signs was only a kind of sorcery.

(p-124) Al-Zamakhshari said: "Awa lam yakfuru" (Did they not disbelieve) means the fathers of their kind, and whoever holds their creed shares their creed, and their obstinacy is their obstinacy; they are the disbelievers of the time of Musa, "bima utiya Musa" (in what was given to Musa). And from al-Hasan: there was already a basis among the Arabs in the days of Musa, so its meaning according to this is: Did not their fathers disbelieve? They said of Musa and Harun: "Two sorceries that back each other up" (saahiran tazaharaa), that is, they cooperated. End of quotation. "Min qablu" (before): it may be connected to "yakfuru" and to "utiya."

The majority read: "saahiran" (two sorcerers). Mujahid said: Musa and Harun. Al-Hasan said: Musa and Isa. Ibn Abbas said: Musa and Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-Hasan also said: Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud], Zayd ibn Ali, and the Kufans read: "sihraan" (two magics). Ibn Abbas said: the Torah and the Qur'an. It was also said: the Torah and the Injil, or Musa and Harun were called two magics as a form of emphasis.

"Tazaharaa" means they cooperated. The majority read "tazaharaa" as a past verb on the pattern of tafaa'ala. Ibn Khalawayh said: its shaddah is a grammatical error, because it is a past verb, and the shaddah is only used in the present tense. Sahib al-Lawami said: I do not know its basis. If it were read "yazzaharaa" with a ya', taking into account "saahiraan," it would have a basis, or by estimating "they two are sorcerers that back each other up."

"Wa qaluu inna bikullin kaafiruun" (And they said: Indeed we disbelieve in each of them), that is, in each of the two sorcerers or the two sorceries. Then Allah commanded him to proclaim this verse, which is His saying: "Qul fa'tuu" (Say: Then bring), that is, you, O deniers of these books, which contain the command to acts of worship and noble character, forbid disbelief and blameworthy traits, and for which Allah promised great reward. "If your denial is for some reason, then bring a Book from Allah which gives better guidance than these two, I will follow it with you." It is also permissible that the condition is intended as mockery of them. Zayd ibn Ali read "atta'bi'uhu" with a raf' on the 'ayn as a new sentence, meaning: I follow it.

"Fa-in lam yastajiibuu laka" (And if they do not respond to you). Ibn Abbas said: it means if they do not believe in what you have brought of proofs, and they are not able to bring a Book that is better. Or the saying "fa'tuu bikitab" may itself be the call, since it is a request from them and a call upon them to bring it. It is known that they will not respond by bringing a Book from Allah. Al-Zamakhshari said: al-gharb is the place lying on the western side, which is the place where Moses' appointed time on the Mount occurred, and where Allah wrote for him on the tablets. The command decreed to Moses is the revelation that was revealed to him. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: you were not present at the place where We revealed to Moses, nor were you among the company of those who witnessed the revelation to him, or [witnessing] upon the revelation to him, namely his deputies whom he chose for the appointed time, so that you might learn from the body of the witnesses what happened to Moses at his appointed time, the writing of the Torah for him on the tablets, and other things.

(If you ask): how does His saying ﴿But We produced generations﴾ connect with this statement, and in what respect is it a corrective (istidrak) to it? (I answer): its connection to it and its being a corrective lies in the fact that its meaning is: But We produced, after the era of the revelation until your era, many generations, so the lifetime stretched over the last of them, and that is the generation in which you exist.

﴿The lifetime grew long﴾: that is, the period of the cessation of revelation, and the sciences were effaced, so it became necessary to send you to them. So We sent you and taught you knowledge of the stories of the prophets and the story of Moses. It is as if He said: you were not a witness to Moses and what happened to him, but We revealed it to you. Thus He mentioned the cause of the revelation, which is the lengthening of the interval, and indicated the effect through it, in accordance with Allah's custom of brevity. Therefore this istidrak (corrective statement) resembles the two istidraks after it.

﴿And you were not dwelling﴾: that is, residing among the people of Madyan, who were Shu'ayb and the believers.

﴿Reciting to them Our verses﴾: reading to them, learning from them, meaning the verses in which is the story of Shu'ayb and his people. But We sent you and informed you of them and taught them to you.

﴿When We called out﴾: he means the calling out to Moses on the night of the secret conversation and speaking with him. But We taught you. It has been said: ﴿So the lifetime grew long for them﴾ and prophethood became dormant, the laws were effaced, and much of them was distorted. The completion of the statement is implied, and its estimate is: We sent you renewing those reports, distinguishing the truth from what had been disputed among them, as a mercy from Us. It has been said: it is possible that the meaning is: you were not among the witnesses at that time, and between you and Moses there were generations whose lifetimes stretched long, and you now relate those circumstances by way of direct witnessing and vision, through Our inspiration to you as a miracle for you. It has been said: "tatlu" (reciting) is a circumstantial clause (hal), and it has been said: it is a new independent statement, meaning: you now recite the story of Shu'ayb, but We sent you as a messenger, and We sent down to you a Book in which these forgotten reports are contained, which you recite to them, and had it not been for you, I would not have informed them of what they did not witness.

Al-Farra' said: ﴿And you were not dwelling﴾ among the people of Madyan with Moses, so that you would see him and hear his speech, and now you are ﴿reciting to them Our verses﴾, that is, to your community, so it is disconnected [from what precedes]. End of quotation. It has been said: if he was not present at that place, then what is the meaning of ﴿nor were you among the witnesses﴾? Ibn 'Abbas said: the estimate is: you did not attend that place, and even had you attended, you would not have witnessed those events, for it is possible that there was [someone] there who would neither witness nor see. Muqatil said: he did not witness the people of Madyan so as to read their report to the people of Makkah, but We sent you to the people of Makkah, and sent down to you these reports, and had it not been for that, you would not have known. Al-Dahhak said: he says: you, O Muhammad, were not the messenger to the people of Madyan, reciting to them the verses of the Book, but rather it was another, (p-123) but We were ever sending a messenger in every age: We sent Shu'ayb to Madyan, and We sent you to the Arabs so that you would be the seal of the prophets. End of quotation.

Al-Tabari said: ﴿When We called out﴾ with [the words]: "I will write it for those who fear [Me]." And from Abu Hurayrah: that at that time a voice was called out from heaven: "O community of Muhammad, I have answered you before you called upon Me, and I have forgiven you before you asked Me." Then Moses (peace be upon him) said: "O Allah, make me of the community of Muhammad." So the meaning is: when We called out by Your command, and We informed you of your prophethood.

The majority read ﴿mercy﴾ in the accusative (raḥmatan), so it is estimated: "but We made you a mercy," and it is estimated: We informed you and made you aware as a mercy. 'Isa and Abu Haywah read it in the nominative (raḥmatun), and they estimated: "but he is a mercy," or "he is a mercy," or "you are a mercy."

﴿That you might warn a people to whom no warner had come﴾: that is, in the period of the interval between you and 'Isa, which is about five hundred and fifty years or so. The answer to (lawla) is omitted. The meaning is: had it not been that they would say, when they are punished for what they had sent forth of polytheism and sins, "Why did You not send to us a messenger?", arguing with that against us, [We sent messengers]. That is: We only sent the messengers to remove this excuse, as He said: ﴿So that there would not be for people any argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165], and [so that] you would not say: ﴿There came to us no bringer of good tidings nor warner﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 19]. The estimate of the answer is: We did not send messengers to them, this is the statement of al-Zajjaj. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: its estimate is: We would have hastened to punish them with what they deserve.

The misfortune (muṣība) is the punishment. Since most actions are performed by the hands, every deed was expressed by the earning of the hands, even deeds of the hearts, as an extension of speech, and making the minority follow the majority, and giving the majority precedence over the minority.

The fa' in ﴿fa-yaqulu﴾ is for conjunction with "tuṣība" [it might befall them]; the second lawla is for urging (taḥḍīḍ). And in "fa-nattabi'a" the fa' is the answer to the urging.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you ask): how is this meaning valid, when the punishment has been made the cause of the sending, not the saying, since the particle of prevention (ḥarf al-imtina') enters upon it and not upon the saying? (I answer): the saying is what is intended, so that it would be the cause of the sending of the messengers, but since the punishment was the cause of the saying, its existence was dependent upon its existence. The punishment was made as if it were the cause of the sending through the medium of the saying. Thus lawla was placed before it, and the saying was brought joined to it by the fa' which gives the meaning of causation. Its meaning reduces to your saying: "And had it not been for their saying this, ﴿when a misfortune befalls them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 156], We would not have sent [messengers]." But this method was chosen for a subtle reason, which is that they were not punished, for example, for their disbelief, while they had seen what they were compelled by to the certain knowledge. They did not say: "Why did You not send to us a messenger?", and the cause of this saying of theirs is only the punishment and nothing else, not regret over what they missed of faith in their Creator. In this there is, of the strong testimony to the firmness and deep-rootedness of their disbelief, what is not hidden, like their saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would go back to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. End of quotation.

As for "al-Haqq" (the Truth): it is the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who came with the inimitable Book which cut off their excuses. It has been said: it is the Qur'an.

﴿Like what was given to Moses﴾. ﴿Before﴾: that is, before the Book that was sent down all at once, and the turning of the staff into a serpent, the splitting of the sea, and other signs. They proposed that out of obstinacy and stubbornness, just as they said: "Why was not a treasure sent down upon him?" and other such proposals they made. This statement that they uttered is from the teaching of the Jews to the Quraysh; they said to them: "Will he not bring a manifest sign like the signs of Moses?" So Allah answered them that they disbelieved in the signs of Moses, and what occurred from them concerning the signs of Moses is what occurred from these [people] concerning the signs of the Messenger.

The pronoun in ﴿Did they not disbelieve﴾ refers to the Jews, as Ibn 'Atiyyah said. It has been said: the speaker of that is the Arabs, by instruction, as we have said. It has been said: the speaker of that is the Jews. It appears to me that it refers to the Quraysh, who said: "Why was he not given (*lawla ūtiya*)," meaning Muhammad, "the like of what was given to Moses?" That is because their denial of Muhammad (ﷺ) is a denial of Moses (peace be upon him), and their attribution of sorcery to the Messenger is like their attribution of sorcery to Moses, since the prophets are of one valley. Whoever attributes to one of the prophets what is not fitting has attributed it to all the prophets. All the pronouns harmonise in this, in His saying: ﴿Say, "Then bring a Book from Allah"﴾. Although the apparent meaning of "qala" (saying) is verbal utterance, it may also apply to belief, and they, in terms of denying prophethoods, believed that what appeared at the hands of the prophets of signs was only a kind of sorcery.

(p-124) Al-Zamakhshari said: "Awa lam yakfuru" (Did they not disbelieve) means the fathers of their kind, and whoever holds their creed shares their creed, and their obstinacy is their obstinacy; they are the disbelievers of the time of Musa, "bima utiya Musa" (in what was given to Musa). And from al-Hasan: there was already a basis among the Arabs in the days of Musa, so its meaning according to this is: Did not their fathers disbelieve? They said of Musa and Harun: "Two sorceries that back each other up" (saahiran tazaharaa), that is, they cooperated. End of quotation. "Min qablu" (before): it may be connected to "yakfuru" and to "utiya."

The majority read: "saahiran" (two sorcerers). Mujahid said: Musa and Harun. Al-Hasan said: Musa and Isa. Ibn Abbas said: Musa and Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-Hasan also said: Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud], Zayd ibn Ali, and the Kufans read: "sihraan" (two magics). Ibn Abbas said: the Torah and the Qur'an. It was also said: the Torah and the Injil, or Musa and Harun were called two magics as a form of emphasis.

"Tazaharaa" means they cooperated. The majority read "tazaharaa" as a past verb on the pattern of tafaa'ala. Talhah and al-A'mash read "izzaharaa" with a hamzat al-wasl and a shaddah on the zay, and likewise it is in the reading of Abdullah; its original form is "tazaharaa," and the ta' was assimilated into the za', so a hamzat al-wasl was brought in because of the sukun of the assimilated ta'. Mahbub from al-Hasan, Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Dhimari, Abu Haywa, and Abu Khallad from al-Yazidi read "tazzaharaa" with a ta' and a shaddah on the za'. Ibn Khalawayh said: its shaddah is a grammatical error, because it is a past verb, and the shaddah is only used in the present tense. Sahib al-Lawami said: I do not know its basis. Sahib al-Kamil fi al-Qira'at said: it has no meaning. End of quotation. However, it has an explanation in the language: it is a present tense verb from which the nun has been dropped, and the dropping of it has occurred in a few instances in speech and in poetry. "Saahiran" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: "antuma saahiraani tatazaharaani" (you two are two sorcerers who back each other up); then the ta' was assimilated into the za' and the nun was dropped, and the pronoun of address was observed. If it were read "yazzaharaa" with a ya', taking into account "saahiraan," it would have a basis, or by estimating "they two are sorcerers that back each other up."

"Wa qaluu inna bikullin kaafiruun" (And they said: Indeed we disbelieve in each of them), that is, in each of the two sorcerers or the two sorceries. Then Allah commanded him to proclaim this verse, which is His saying: "Qul fa'tuu" (Say: Then bring), that is, you, O deniers of these books, which contain the command to acts of worship and noble character, forbid disbelief and blameworthy traits, and for which Allah promised great reward. "If your denial is for some reason, then bring a Book from Allah which gives better guidance than these two, I will follow it with you." The pronoun in "minhaa" refers to what was revealed to Musa and to Muhammad (ﷺ) (may Allah bless them both and grant them peace). Making their bringing of such a book conditional on truthfulness is a matter that is certain and established: it will not happen, and their truthfulness is impossible, just as it is impossible that they bring a Book from Allah that is more guided than the two Books. It is also permissible that the condition is intended as mockery of them. Zayd ibn Ali read "atta'bi'uhu" with a raf' on the 'ayn as a new sentence, meaning: I follow it.

"Fa-in lam yastajiibuu laka" (And if they do not respond to you). Ibn Abbas said: it means if they do not believe in what you have brought of proofs, and they are not able to bring a Book that is better. Istijabah (responding) implies a call, and he (ﷺ) always calls to faith; that is, if they do not respond to you after the miracles contained in your Book that was revealed have become clear to them. Or the saying "fa'tuu bikitab" may itself be the call, since it is a request from them and a call upon them to bring it. It is known that they will not respond by bringing a Book from Allah. So know that they have nothing but the following of mere desire, not the following of evidence. "Istajaba" means "ajaba," and it is transitive to the one called with "li" and without it, as He said: "Fastajaba lahu rabbuhu" (Yusuf 34), "Fastajabnaa lahu wa wahabnaa lahu Yahyaa" (al-Anbiya 90), "Fa-in lam yastajiibuu lakum" (Hud 14). The poet said:

"Fa lam yastajibhu 'inda dhaalika mujiibu"
So he transitively used it without "li." Al-Zamakhshari said: this verb is transitive to the call and to the one called with "li," and the call is usually omitted when it is transitive to the one called, so one says: "Istajaba Allahu du'aahu" and "istajaba lahu," but one hardly says "istajaba lahu du'aahu." As for the verse, its meaning is: "lam yastajib du'aa'," with the omission of the modifier. End of quotation.

"Wa man adallu" (And who is more astray), that is, no one is more astray. "Bi-ghayri hudan" (without guidance) is in the position of a circumstantial clause, and this circumstance is a restriction on following desire, because a person may follow what he desires, and that which he desires may contain guidance from Allah, since all desires are divided into those that contain guidance (p-125) and those that do not contain guidance; therefore it is restricted by this circumstance. Al-Zamakhshari said: meaning forsaken, left to his own desire. End of quotation, and this is according to the path of the Mu'tazila.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 28, verses 44–50 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses.﴾ ﴿But We produced generations, and the lifetime grew long for them. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting Our verses to them, but We were ever sending messengers.﴾ ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called out, but it was a mercy from your Lord, that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that perhaps they might be mindful.﴾ ﴿And had it not been that a misfortune might befall them because of what their hands had sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs and be among the believers?"﴾ ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, "Two sorceries backing each other," and they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in both."﴾ ﴿Say, "Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guided than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

When Allah (Exalted) had related the accounts of Moses and the remarkable events that befell him, namely his being conceived at the time when the sons were being slaughtered, his being cast into the sea in a chest, his being returned to his mother, Pharaoh's adoption of him, his being granted judgment and knowledge, his killing of the Copt, his leaving his homeland in flight, his marriage connection with Shu'ayb, his tending of Shu'ayb's sheep for many long years, his return to Egypt, his losing the way, Allah's conversing with him, the manifesting through his hands of those two great miracles, namely the staff and the hand, his being commanded to go to Pharaoh, his dialogue with him, Pharaoh's denial and his destruction along with his people, and the favour bestowed upon Moses in giving him the Torah, Allah (Exalted) revealed all of that to Muhammad, His Messenger (ﷺ). He reminded him of His bounty upon him in this regard, and of the unseen matters that He had specially granted him, which neither he nor his people had known. So He said: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command.﴾

As for "al-amr" (the command), it has been said: it is prophethood and the judgment that Allah gave Moses. It has also been said: the command is the command to Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he should be among his community, and this interpretation harmonises with what follows it, His saying: ﴿But We produced generations.﴾ It has also been said: the command is the destruction of Pharaoh by water, and "bi-janib al-gharbi" (on the western side) is to be understood as the sea (al-yamm).

He began first by negating a specific matter, which is that he was not present (p-122) at the time when Allah decreed the command to Moses. Then he repeated it by saying that he was not among the witnesses. The meaning, and Allah knows best, is: not among the witnesses to all that We informed you of. Thus it is a negation of his witnessing all that happened to Moses, so it was a generality after a specification.

As for "bi-janib al-gharbi": according to some, it is an idafa (construct) of the qualified noun to its qualifier; according to others, the noun has been omitted and the qualifier put in its place. On the first view the original is "bi-l-janib al-gharbi," and on the second the original is "bi-janib al-makan al-gharbi." The preference between the two views is mentioned in grammar (nahw).

As for "al-gharbi": Qatadah said it is the western side of the mountain. Al-Hasan said: Allah sent Moses to the west. Abu 'Ubaydah said: the place where the sun, the moon and the stars set. It has been said: here there is a western mountain. It has been said: al-gharbi is of the valley, and it has been said: of the sea.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: the meaning is: you, O Muhammad, were not present at these unseen matters about which you are informed, but they came to you by Our revelation. That is to say, it was incumbent that one should hasten to believe in you, but the matter stretched over the generations which We produced age after age, so their wisdom faded and their ignorance and error became firmly established.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-gharb is the place lying on the western side, which is the place where Moses' appointed time on the Mount occurred, and where Allah wrote for him on the tablets. The command decreed to Moses is the revelation that was revealed to him. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: you were not present at the place where We revealed to Moses, nor were you among the company of those who witnessed the revelation to him, or [witnessing] upon the revelation to him, namely his deputies whom he chose for the appointed time, so that you might learn from the body of the witnesses what happened to Moses at his appointed time, the writing of the Torah for him on the tablets, and other things.

Whoever attributes to one of the prophets what is not fitting has attributed it to all the prophets. All the pronouns harmonise in this, in His saying: ﴿Say, "Then bring a Book from Allah"﴾.
